key_insight: VideoMaMa++ targets inconsistent foreground extraction between video chunks using a Preserve-and-Refine Token. The goal is to retain the generalization benefits of video diffusion models while making matting more temporally coherent.
problem_solved: Compute-heavy diffusion models process only 6–24 frames at a time. Independently matting these short chunks from coarse masks can produce inconsistencies at chunk boundaries.
method: Build on diffusion-based video matting, which uses pretrained video priors and coarse mask guidance to estimate foreground transparency.
Introduce a Preserve-and-Refine Token to address temporal consistency, as indicated by the title; the truncated abstract does not provide its implementation details.
impact: More consistent chunked matting could improve foreground extraction for video editing and compositing. The supplied excerpt does not establish measured quality gains or inference costs.
visual_elements: A video timeline divided into 6–24-frame chunks, with boundary inconsistencies highlighted.
A conceptual diagram showing the Preserve-and-Refine Token connecting adjacent chunks.
A frame sequence illustrating the desired reduction in foreground-edge flicker.
A simple pipeline: video and coarse masks → diffusion-based matting → foreground transparency.
paper_title: VideoMaMa++: Temporally Consistent Video Matting via Preserve-and-Refine Token
paper_authors: Sangbeom Lim, Seoung Wug Oh, Heeji Yoon, Seungryong Kim, Joon-Young Lee
